newsitem.title: USA: Security alarm at Jewish building in U.S. capital.
newsitem.headline: Security alarm at Jewish building in U.S. capital.

text.p: A mailed package holding suspicious "biological material" sparked a security alert at the headquarters of the Jewish organisation B'nai B'rith on Friday and police, fire crews, federal agents and military units rushed to the scene.

"We found some biological material and a note that was left with the package," District of Columbia Police Chief Larry Soulsby said in a televised interview. Authorities cordoned off several blocks of central Washington not far from the White House and disposal squads moved in to remove the package.

"An 8X10 envelope was found in our mailroom with red liquid coming out of it" late Thursday morning, B'nai B'rith spokeswoman Robin Schwartz-Kreger told Reuters by telephone from inside the building. She said it was accompanied by a "threatening" letter but she did not know the nature of the threats.

Hazardous material experts in blue and white protective suits and gas-masks removed the package from where it had been transferred just outside the building housing B'nai B'rith's international headquarters. An FBI spokeswoman said military experts were handling the removal and the package would be taken to the Bethesda Naval Research Centre for testing.

Police and fire officials said they had not been able to confirm what was in the package or to establish that it was a health hazard. But Soulsby said, "We are very concerned that some of the officers who responded initially as well as others may have been contiminated."

According to initial police reports, only two B'nai B'rith employees had complained of suffering respiratory irritations and they were being treated at the scene. One person was seen outside the building strapped in a medical chair being sprayed with a decontaminant by a white-clad rescue team.
